levels.title: Chemistry in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what chemistry studies: what things are made of and how they change.

levels.title: What Matter Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain matter as anything that has mass and takes up space.

levels.title: Solid, Liquid, Gas
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the three everyday states of matter.

levels.title: Melting and Boiling
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what happens to particles when things melt or boil.

levels.title: Plasma
levels.objective: After this level you can explain plasma, the state of matter in lightning and the Sun.

levels.title: Mixtures and Solutions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how mixtures and solutions differ.

levels.title: Separating Mixtures
levels.objective: After this level you can explain filtering, evaporating and distilling.

levels.title: Density
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why some things float and others sink.

levels.title: Physical or Chemical Change?
levels.objective: After this level you can tell a physical change from a chemical one.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Matter
levels.objective: After this level you can explain states of matter, mixtures and the two kinds of change.

levels.title: The Idea of Atoms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the idea of atoms began with the ancient Greeks.

levels.title: Inside an Atom
levels.objective: After this level you can name protons, neutrons and electrons and where each is found.

levels.title: How Small Is an Atom?
levels.objective: After this level you can picture just how small an atom is.

levels.title: Electron Shells
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how electrons fill shells around the nucleus.

levels.title: Isotopes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain isotopes as atoms of one element with different masses.

levels.title: Radioactivity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain radioactive decay.

levels.title: Carbon Dating
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how carbon dating tells the age of old things.

levels.title: Seeing Atoms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how scientists can image single atoms.

levels.title: Finding the Atom's Parts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Thomson's and Rutherford's experiments.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Atoms
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the parts of an atom and how we discovered them.

levels.title: Elements
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what an element is.

levels.title: Mendeleev's Table
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Mendeleev arranged the elements and predicted new ones.

levels.title: Reading the Periodic Table
levels.objective: After this level you can explain groups and periods on the periodic table.

levels.title: Metals and Nonmetals
levels.objective: After this level you can compare metals and nonmetals.

levels.title: Noble Gases
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why noble gases barely react, and how neon lights glow.

levels.title: Alkali Metals
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why sodium and potassium react so violently with water.

levels.title: Halogens
levels.objective: After this level you can describe chlorine and its relatives and how we use them.

levels.title: Making New Elements
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the heaviest elements are made in laboratories.

levels.title: Elements From Stars
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how stars and supernovas made the elements.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Periodic Table
levels.objective: After this level you can use the periodic table to predict how an element behaves.

levels.title: Hydrogen
levels.objective: After this level you can describe hydrogen, the lightest and most common element.

levels.title: Oxygen
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why oxygen matters for breathing and burning.

levels.title: Carbon
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why carbon is the basis of life.

levels.title: Diamond and Graphite
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how carbon can form both diamond and pencil lead.

levels.title: Iron
levels.objective: After this level you can explain iron's role in steel and in your blood.

levels.title: Gold and Silver
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why gold and silver were prized for money and jewelry.

levels.title: Copper and Bronze
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how bronze began an age of history.

levels.title: Aluminum
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why aluminum was once more precious than gold.

levels.title: Silicon
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why silicon runs our computers.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Elements Up Close
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the properties and uses of common elements.

levels.title: Molecules

levels.title: Salt and Ionic Bonds

levels.title: Covalent Bonds

levels.title: Metallic Bonds
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why metals conduct electricity and bend without breaking.

levels.title: Crystals
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how crystals form.

levels.title: Polymers

levels.title: Chemical Formulas
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a formula like H2O describes a molecule.

levels.title: Shapes of Molecules

levels.title: Milestone: Atoms to Molecules
levels.objective: After this level you can connect atoms, elements and bonds into one picture of matter.

levels.title: What a Reaction Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain reactants and products.

levels.title: Burning

levels.title: Rust

levels.title: Fireworks
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how fireworks get their colors.

levels.title: Explosions

levels.title: Checkpoint: Reactions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what happens in a chemical reaction and what controls its speed.

levels.title: Acid Rain
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what causes acid rain.

levels.objective: After this level you can explain how extra carbon dioxide affects the oceans.

levels.title: Batteries
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how chemistry makes electricity in a battery.

levels.title: Stomach Acid
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the stomach uses strong acid safely.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Acids and Bases
levels.objective: After this level you can explain acids, bases and the pH scale with everyday examples.

levels.title: Proteins

levels.objective: After this level you can explain how soap lifts away grease.

levels.title: Glass From Sand

levels.title: Fuels

levels.objective: After this level you can explain the chemistry behind cooking, cleaning and everyday materials.
